feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: The latest in space science: We look back at the Big Bang
entry.summary: In this edition of Spacing Out, the team from Short Wave shares the latest developments in space science, including the theory on why the universe is made of matter

entry.title: A new study gives us a clearer picture on how many people have been deported
entry.summary: Cracking down on immigration has been the centerpiece of the Trump administration, but the government has limited the public's access to the numbers. A new study gives us a clearer picture.

entry.title: Merck and Moderna release promising data on cancer vaccine trial
entry.summary: A study of a personalized vaccine combined with an existing immunotherapy found the treatment helped patients with melanoma avoid cancer recurrence. The combination trains the patient's immune system to go after cancer cells.

entry.title: At a Texas high school football game, fans offer a glimpse into evolving politics
entry.summary: We talk with voters at a Texas high school football game at the tailgate, in line at the concession booth and in the stands to hear about the issues that matter to Texans this cycle.

entry.title: Video released in Mississippi police shooting of toddler
entry.summary: The police officer involved in a shooting in Mississippi and killed a toddler has resigned a day after video of the incident was released.

entry.title: Father who killed the Bend school shooter speaks to Oregon Public Broadcasting
entry.summary: Kaylub Giamanco, the father who shot the 16-year-old who opened fire on a Bend, Ore., elementary school and killed three kids and a teacher, shares what he wants people to know about his experience.

entry.title: Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms
entry.summary: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.

entry.title: What we learned (and didn't) about Elizabeth Holmes in 'You Can See Everything'
entry.summary: You Can See Everything, isn't a straightforward documentary. NPR tech reporter Bobby Allyn and pop culture critic Linda Holmes discuss what they took away from the film by comedian Nathan Fielder.

entry.title: Israeli PM pledges massive military operation after West Bank checkpoint attack
entry.summary: Israel's Prime Minister is vowing to launch a major military operation in the West Bank in response to an attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli military checkpoint that killed two soldiers.

entry.title: Songs by Adela, Karol G and Dominic Fike make waves on the Billboard charts
entry.summary: Taylor Swift still has the No. 1 song in the country, but there are several songs behind her worth your attention.
